header.name: Theory of modern cryptography
header.description: In this course, we will discuss the theoretical foundations of cryptography. It is one of the most important areas of computer science, and the applications of cryptography are ubiquitous in the digital age. There are various aspects of cryptography, but we will mainly focus on encryption, which deals with communicating securely in the presence of a malicious party. In the first half of this course, we will cover various mathematical concepts that guarantee the securities of existing cryptographic systems, like perfect secrecy, one-way functions, hard-core predicates, pseudorandom generators, pseudorandom permutations and functions, trapdoor one-way functions, etc. We will spend most of our time in this part on pseudorandomness, where we will cover various important properties like an “equivalence” of one-way functions and pseudorandom generators, the unpredictability of a pseudorandom generator, etc.  Then, in the second half, we will see how to use these mathematical concepts to design some of the important cryptographic systems, like the one-time pad, Data Encryption Standard, Advanced Encryption Standard, the RSA cryptosystem, etc. Towards the end of this course, we will cover the concepts of interactive and zero-knowledge proofs.
prerequisites_desirable: MTH201 or any other introductory course on probability

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Discuss different types of encryption schemes

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Discuss various mathematical tools in modern cryptography

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Explain important results and open problems in modern cryptography

lecture_topics: Introduction to cryptography and encryption scheme
Perfect secrecy - three equivalent definitions and One-time pad
Shannon's theorem on perfect secrecy and introduction to modern cryptography
One-way functions (OWF) - equivalence of strong and weak one-way functions
Candidate one-way functions and hard-core predicates
Increasing the expansion factor of a PRG
Security against Chosen-Plaintext attacks (CPA) and Chosen-Ciphertext attacks(CCA)

A summary report on the content of the course
